text:
Morgan Frost is doing what Calgary got him to do: drive offense from the middle without a lot of help. He has 12 points in 19 games, six on the power play, and his scoring rate per hour sits above what our numbers expect from him. Goals are almost exactly in line with his chances (4 on 3.9 expected), so there's no luck to strip out.

The concern is volume. Over the last ten games he has one goal and only 1.0 expected goals of his own; the assists (five) are carrying the line. His shot is not a weapon either, in the 14th percentile for top speed by NHL Edge.

Where he hurts teams is in transition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his shots coming off the rush last season, and Evolving-Hockey rated him 73rd of 401 forwards in value despite weaker linemates. With headlines asking what the Flames should do with him, the question is less about his game than his fit.
headline: Frost keeps the Flames' power play moving
